zh.summary: 分清掃描線索、已確認弱點、可利用性與入侵證據，依授權安排驗證、修補及複測。

sourceBody.text: 先記住這一課最重要的觀念：
弱點評估（Vulnerability Assessment, VA）是找出安全問題、判斷風險與安排修復；滲透測試（Penetration Testing, PT）則是在授權範圍內，實際驗證攻擊者可能做到什麼程度。
兩者都在檢查資安，但回答的問題不同。

items: VA：哪裡可能有問題？問題有多嚴重？先修什麼？
PT：這些問題能不能被利用？利用後會造成什麼影響？

sourceBody.text: 一、先用「檢查房屋安全」來理解
假設你買了一間房子，擔心小偷闖入。
第一位：弱點評估人員（VA）
他檢查門鎖、窗戶、監視器和警報器，發現後門的鎖已經老舊，可能容易被打開。
他會告訴你：「後門鎖有安全疑慮，建議優先更換。」
第二位：滲透測試人員（PT）
你明確授權他在不破壞門鎖的條件下，測試後門是否真的容易被繞過。
他成功打開門，證明「這個缺陷在特定條件下可以被利用」。
這裡有一個重要差別：
VA 發現「門鎖可能不安全」，不等於有人真的開得了門。
PT 成功開門，也不代表以前已經有小偷闖入。
這就是資安工作中非常重要的原則：可能有漏洞、漏洞可被利用、系統已遭攻擊，是三種不同的結論。
二、六個資安名詞，一次搞懂
現在我們把房屋換成一個購物網站。
網站有 10,000 名會員，每個會員只能查看自己的訂單。

visual.caption: 圖 1｜資產、弱點、威脅、利用、攻擊與風險
visual.description: 資產可能存在弱點；威脅與利用方法是不同概念。攻擊是否發生須另有證據；風險綜合發生可能性與損失，不是必然發生的最後一步。

items.title: Asset｜資產
items.body: 會員資料、訂單、系統服務

items.title: Vulnerability｜弱點
items.body: 會員 A 可能讀到會員 B 的訂單

items.title: Threat｜威脅
items.body: 有人想竊取不屬於自己的資料

items.title: Exploit｜利用方法
items.body: 透過某種請求方式觸發權限缺陷

items.title: Attack｜攻擊
items.body: 實際嘗試利用漏洞存取訂單

items.title: Risk｜風險
items.body: 評估這種事件發生的可能性及造成的損失

sourceBody.text: 這是一張概念關係圖，並不是說所有弱點必然經歷每個階段。即使攻擊尚未發生，系統也可能已經存在風險。
特別注意 Risk（風險）不等於 Vulnerability（弱點）。
假設兩台電腦存在完全相同的漏洞：
第一台是與網際網路直接連接、儲存大量客戶資料的正式伺服器。第二台是完全隔離、沒有真實資料的實驗機。
漏洞可能相同，但兩者的暴露程度、攻擊可能性與損害可能非常不同，因此修復優先順序也可能不同。
三、弱點掃描、弱點評估、滲透測試有什麼差別？
這是 CEH 考試與實務最容易混淆的地方。

rows: 核對問題、判斷風險、安排修復
在授權範圍內驗證攻擊路徑
實際可能造成什麼影響？

sourceBody.text: 想像看醫生：掃描像是健康檢查儀器出現異常數值；弱點評估像是醫師結合檢查結果、病史與其他證據做判斷；滲透測試則是針對特定疑慮，安排受控的進一步驗證。
但這只是類比，不代表 VA 一定不能做實際測試，或 PT 一定不使用掃描工具。真正的差別在於工作目的、證據要求與授權範圍。
四、實際案例：掃描器說有高危漏洞，你應該怎麼辦？
假設你負責醫院內部的一套 AI 影像分析系統。
系統提供 Web 介面，供授權的醫療人員登入、上傳測試影像和查看分析結果。
某天，你用經過授權的弱點掃描器檢查系統，得到：

visual.caption: 圖 2｜疑似高嚴重度漏洞：待確認
visual.description: 示意掃描結果，並非真實檢測。版本資訊是線索，尚未確認漏洞或利用成功。

items.title: 偵測資訊
items.body: Web 服務版本 2.4

items.title: 工具判斷
items.body: 可能符合某項已知漏洞的版本條件

items.title: 實際利用
items.body: 尚未驗證

sourceBody.text: 這個時候你能直接說「醫院 AI 系統有高危漏洞」嗎？
還不能直接當成已確認的結論。
第一步：確認工具有沒有看錯
掃描器可能只是讀取伺服器回傳的版本資訊。例如它看到 `2.4`，就推測這個版本可能有問題。
但事實上，系統可能早已套用安全修補程式，只是對外顯示的版本字串沒有改變。
因此，你需要確認實際套件、修補紀錄、受影響的功能及漏洞成立條件。
這是在排除 False Positive（誤報）。
第二步：確認漏洞有沒有實際風險
假設漏洞真的存在，接下來還需要問：
漏洞需要先登入嗎？外部網路接觸得到嗎？需要特殊權限嗎？成功利用會影響哪些資料？
掃描器的高嚴重度警告值得關注，但不等於每個部署環境都具有相同風險。
第三步：必要時進行授權滲透測試
如果醫院需要知道權限漏洞是否真的能導致越權存取，就要先確認測試授權。
例如僅在測試環境中建立兩個帳號：

visual.caption: 圖 3｜兩個測試帳號與允許／拒絕案例
visual.description: 測試目的：確認伺服器是否真的依照登入身分執行資源存取控制。這裡列的是政策預期，並非已執行結果。

items.title: 帳號 A
items.body: 測試影像紀錄 A001

items.title: 帳號 B
items.body: 測試影像紀錄 B001

items.title: A 讀取自己的 A001
items.body: 允許

items.title: A 嘗試讀取 B 的 B001
items.body: 應拒絕

sourceBody.text: 如果帳號 A 真的成功讀取 B 的測試資料，你就獲得了比版本警告更強的證據：在這次測試條件下，確實發生了越權存取。
這類問題在 Web 安全中稱為 Broken Access Control（存取控制失效），可能涉及 IDOR（Insecure Direct Object Reference，不安全的直接物件參照）。
但它仍不能證明過去有人入侵，也不能直接證明所有資料都能讀取。
第四步：修補之後，還要複測
修補不是只看工程師說「已經改好」。
需要重新驗證：A 能不能正常看 A001？A 是否已無法讀取 B001？其他合法功能是否仍正常？
這稱為 Retesting（複測）。前者驗證功能沒有被修壞，後者驗證權限問題確實得到改善。
五、完整的資安工作流程

visual.caption: 圖 4｜從授權到修補複測的五步工作流程
visual.description: 第四步須視需求及授權決定；五個節點表示工作順序，不表示每次都必須執行漏洞利用。

items.title: 確認測試授權與範圍
items.body: 指定系統、時段、帳號、可使用的方法、禁止事項與停止條件。

items.title: 蒐集線索
items.body: 使用掃描、設定檢查、程式檢閱等方式發現疑似弱點。

items.title: 核對與分析
items.body: 確認是否真的存在、影響哪些資產、風險有多高。

items.title: 必要時進行受控驗證
items.body: 只有在授權涵蓋的情況下，才進一步測試可利用性與影響。

items.title: 修補並複測
items.body: 保留原始證據、修改紀錄與驗證結果。

sourceBody.text: 其中最重要的文件之一叫做 ROE（Rules of Engagement，交戰規則）。
你可以把它想成測試人員與系統所有者簽訂的工作界線：允許測什麼、不准碰什麼、遇到異常要通知誰，以及什麼情況必須停止。
即使你已經找到一個可能的漏洞，也不代表你可以自行擴大測試範圍。
六、CEH 最需要建立的三種判斷能力
第一，學會區分觀察與推論。
「掃描器顯示版本 2.4」是觀察；「這個版本可能存在漏洞」是推論；「系統已經被駭客入侵」則需要完全不同的事件證據。
第二，不要把高嚴重度直接當成最高修復優先順序。
除了漏洞本身嚴重程度，也要考慮系統暴露情況、利用條件、資產價值、既有防護與業務影響。例如一個可從網際網路接觸、已知容易被利用的漏洞，往往需要比隔離系統中難以觸發的缺陷更緊急處理。
第三，理解資安的目的不只是找到漏洞，而是降低風險。
只發現 100 個警告，但沒有驗證、修補或降低風險，並不能直接代表防護變好。
一份有價值的資安報告，應讓負責人知道哪些問題已確認、證據有哪些、應先處理什麼，以及修補後如何確認有效。
七、理解檢核：用 CEH 分析師的角度思考
假設你檢查一套公司內部系統，弱點掃描器指出一項高嚴重度漏洞。你尚未確認修補狀態，也沒有進一步執行滲透測試的授權。
問題一：最合理的下一步是什麼？
A. 直接執行漏洞利用程式，確認能不能成功。
B. 告訴主管系統已被駭客入侵。
C. 先確認產品、修補狀態與漏洞成立條件，再決定是否申請進一步測試。
D. 沒看到資料外洩，就忽略警告。
問題二：用自己的話回答
假設滲透測試成功讀取一筆不屬於測試帳號的合成資料，這個結果可以證明什麼？又有哪些事情還不能證明？

paragraphs: 問題一答案 C。先核對產品、修補及漏洞成立條件；進一步測試須取得授權。A 超出目前授權；B 把掃描警告誤當入侵證據；D 把尚未看到外洩誤當沒有風險。
問題二：若政策明定帳號不可讀取該筆資料，成功讀取能證明本次帳號、環境及請求條件下發生越權存取。不能因此推論所有資料都可讀取、正式環境同樣受影響或過去曾遭入侵。保存請求／回覆、帳號、時間、合成資料與預期政策，修補後同時複測合法讀取成功及越權讀取被拒絕。

sourceBody.text: 這一課的核心能力，就是把「發現疑似漏洞」、「確認存在漏洞」、「證明可被利用」與「證明曾遭入侵」清楚分開。這不只是 CEH 考試觀念，也是實際撰寫資安評估報告時不可混淆的證據層級。
來源與延伸閱讀

[NIST SP 800-115：資訊安全測試與評估](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final) 說明測試規劃、技術限制與改善流程。[OWASP：不安全的直接物件參照防護](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) 說明逐物件授權檢查。本文房屋、購物網站及醫院案例均為合成教學情境，版本 2.4 不對應特定產品或 CVE。

en.summary: Separate scanner clues, confirmed vulnerabilities, exploitability and incident evidence; plan authorized validation, remediation and retesting.

sourceBody.text: Start with the central idea of this lesson:

Vulnerability assessment (VA) finds security problems, evaluates risk and plans remediation. Penetration testing (PT) works within an authorized scope to validate what an attacker might actually achieve.
Both examine security, but they answer different questions.

items: VA: Where might the problems be? How serious are they? What should be fixed first?
PT: Can these problems be exploited? What impact would exploitation have?

sourceBody.text: 1. Understand the difference through a home-security inspection
Suppose you buy a house and worry about burglary.
First professional: the vulnerability assessor (VA)
They inspect locks, windows, cameras and alarms, and discover that the rear-door lock is old and may be easy to open.
They tell you: “The rear-door lock raises a security concern. Replace it as a priority.”
Second professional: the penetration tester (PT)
You explicitly authorize them to test whether the rear door can really be bypassed without damaging the lock.
They open the door successfully, demonstrating that this defect can be exploited under particular conditions.
There is an important distinction here:
VA finding that a lock may be insecure does not prove that someone can actually open the door.
PT successfully opening it also does not prove that a burglar entered in the past.
This is an essential evidence principle in security work: a suspected vulnerability, an exploitable vulnerability and a compromised system are three different conclusions.
2. Understand six security terms together
Now replace the house with an online shop.
The shop has 10,000 members, and each member should be able to view only their own orders.

visual.caption: Figure 1 | Assets, vulnerabilities, threats, exploits, attacks and risk
visual.description: An asset may have a vulnerability. A threat and an exploit are distinct concepts. An attack requires separate evidence; risk combines likelihood and loss rather than being an inevitable final stage.

items.title: Asset
items.body: Member data, orders and system services

items.title: Vulnerability
items.body: Member A may be able to read member B’s orders

items.title: Threat
items.body: Someone wants to steal data that does not belong to them

items.title: Exploit
items.body: A request method that triggers an authorization defect

items.title: Attack
items.body: An actual attempt to exploit the defect to access orders

items.title: Risk
items.body: Assessment of event likelihood and resulting loss

sourceBody.text: This is a concept relationship diagram, not a claim that every vulnerability inevitably passes through every stage. Risk may exist before any attack occurs.
In particular, risk is not the same as a vulnerability.
Suppose two computers have exactly the same vulnerability:
One is an internet-facing production server storing extensive customer data. The other is an entirely isolated lab computer with no real data.
The vulnerability may be identical, but exposure, attack likelihood and possible damage can differ substantially. Remediation priorities can therefore differ too.
3. How do scanning, assessment and penetration testing differ?
This distinction is easy to confuse in CEH study and in practice.

rows: Use tools to locate suspicious conditions
Verify findings, assess risk and arrange remediation
Which findings are real, and what should be fixed first?
Validate attack paths within an authorized scope
What impact can actually be demonstrated?

sourceBody.text: Think of a medical visit: scanning resembles a screening instrument reporting an abnormal value; assessment resembles a clinician combining that result with history and other evidence; penetration testing resembles a controlled follow-up investigation into a specific concern.
This is only an analogy. It does not mean VA can never perform practical tests or PT never uses scanners. The important differences are purpose, evidence requirements and authorized scope.
4. A practical case: what should you do when a scanner reports a high-severity vulnerability?
Suppose you manage an internal AI imaging-analysis system at a hospital.
It provides a web interface where authorized medical staff sign in, upload test images and view analysis results.
One day, an authorized vulnerability scan reports the following:

visual.caption: Figure 2 | Suspected high-severity vulnerability: unconfirmed
visual.description: Illustrative scanner output, not a real assessment. Version information is a clue; neither vulnerability presence nor successful exploitation is confirmed.

items.title: Detected information
items.body: Web service version 2.4

items.title: Tool inference
items.body: May match version conditions for a known vulnerability

items.title: Exploitation
items.body: Not yet validated

sourceBody.text: Can you immediately state that the hospital AI system has a high-severity vulnerability?
You cannot yet treat that as a confirmed conclusion.
Step 1: Check whether the tool is mistaken
The scanner may only have read a version string returned by the server. For example, seeing `2.4` may lead it to infer that the version could be affected.
The system may already have security patches installed while continuing to display the same version string.
Check the actual package, patch records, affected functionality and conditions required for the vulnerability to exist.
This helps rule out a false positive: a reported problem that is not actually present.
Step 2: Check the vulnerability's practical risk
If the vulnerability really exists, ask further questions:
Does it require signing in? Is it reachable from an external network? Does it require special privileges? Which data would exploitation affect?
A high-severity scanner alert deserves attention, but it does not imply the same risk in every deployment environment.
Step 3: Conduct authorized penetration testing if necessary
If the hospital needs to know whether an authorization defect permits unauthorized access, first establish the testing authorization.
For example, create only two synthetic accounts in a test environment:

visual.caption: Figure 3 | Two test accounts and positive/negative cases
visual.description: Purpose: check whether the server enforces resource access control according to the signed-in identity. These are policy expectations, not observed test results.

items.title: Account A
items.body: Test imaging record A001

items.title: Account B
items.body: Test imaging record B001

items.title: A reads its own A001
items.body: Allow

items.title: A attempts to read B’s B001
items.body: Must deny

sourceBody.text: If account A successfully reads B's test data, you have stronger evidence than a version warning: unauthorized access occurred under these test conditions.
This is called broken access control in web security and may involve an insecure direct object reference (IDOR).
It still does not prove that someone intruded in the past or that all data is readable.
Step 4: Retest after remediation
Remediation is not established simply because an engineer says “it is fixed.”
Verify again: can A still read A001 normally? Is A now unable to read B001? Do other legitimate functions still work?
This is retesting. The positive case checks that normal functionality has not broken, while the negative case checks that the authorization defect has actually been addressed.
5. The complete security workflow

visual.caption: Figure 4 | Five steps from authorization to remediation and retesting
visual.description: Step 4 depends on need and authorization. The five nodes show working order, not a requirement to exploit a vulnerability in every assessment.

items.title: Confirm authorization and scope
items.body: Specify systems, time windows, accounts, allowed methods, prohibited actions and stop conditions.

items.title: Gather clues
items.body: Use scanning, configuration checks and code review to discover suspected vulnerabilities.

items.title: Verify and analyze
items.body: Confirm presence, affected assets and risk.

items.title: Perform controlled validation if needed
items.body: Test exploitability and impact only when covered by authorization.

items.title: Remediate and retest
items.body: Retain original evidence, change records and validation results.

sourceBody.text: One of the most important documents is the rules of engagement (ROE).
Think of it as an agreed working boundary between the tester and system owner: what may be tested, what must not be touched, whom to notify if something goes wrong, and when testing must stop.
Finding a potential vulnerability does not authorize you to expand the testing scope on your own.
6. Three judgments CEH learners need to develop
First, distinguish observations from inferences.
“The scanner displays version 2.4” is an observation. “This version may contain a vulnerability” is an inference. “The system has been compromised” requires entirely different incident evidence.
Second, do not automatically make high severity the highest remediation priority.

Alongside intrinsic severity, consider exposure, exploitation conditions, asset value, existing safeguards and business impact. An internet-reachable vulnerability known to be readily exploitable often needs more urgent attention than a hard-to-trigger defect in an isolated system.
Third, understand that the purpose of security work is to reduce risk, not merely find vulnerabilities.
Finding 100 alerts without validation, remediation or risk reduction does not itself demonstrate better protection.
A useful security report tells the responsible person which issues are confirmed, what evidence supports them, what to address first and how to verify remediation.
7. Understanding check: think like a CEH analyst
Suppose a scanner reports a high-severity vulnerability in an internal company system. You have not checked patch status and have no authorization for further penetration testing.
Question 1: What is the most reasonable next step?
A. Immediately run an exploit to check whether it succeeds.
B. Tell management the system has already been compromised.
C. Check the product, patch status and required conditions, then decide whether to request authorization for further testing.
D. Ignore the alert because no data leak has been seen.
Question 2: Answer in your own words
Suppose penetration testing successfully reads one synthetic record that does not belong to the test account. What does this demonstrate, and what does it still not demonstrate?

paragraphs: Question 1: C. Verify the product, patch status and required conditions; obtain authorization for further testing. A exceeds current authorization. B mistakes a scanner alert for incident evidence. D mistakes no observed leak for no risk.

Question 2: If policy prohibits this account from reading that record, successful reading demonstrates unauthorized access for this account, environment and request conditions. It does not establish access to all data, the same impact in production or a past intrusion. Retain request/response evidence, account, time, synthetic data and expected policy; after remediation, retest both successful legitimate access and denied unauthorized access.

sourceBody.text: The core skill in this lesson is separating a suspected vulnerability, a confirmed vulnerability, demonstrated exploitability and evidence of a past intrusion. This distinction matters both for CEH concepts and for defensible security-assessment reports.
Sources and further reading

[NIST SP 800-115: Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/115/final) explains planning, technique limitations and mitigation. [OWASP: Insecure Direct Object Reference Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) explains per-object authorization checks. The house, shop and hospital cases are synthetic teaching scenarios. Version 2.4 does not identify a particular product or CVE.
